prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your home, budget, timing, brand preferences, ductwork condition, and whether you want high-efficiency equipment or basic replacement. I can help you pick a great contractor, but first I need a little info. Quick questions:

- What’s your ZIP code or neighborhood in Atlanta?
- Is this a single-family home, condo, or commercial property?
- Roughly how old is the current system and do you have existing ductwork?
- Do you have a brand preference (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman, etc.)?
- Do you want highest efficiency (18+ SEER) or a mid-range replacement (14–16 SEER)?
- Any budget range or need financing?

What I can do for you
- If you give your ZIP code I can list well-reviewed, licensed HVAC companies near you (based on my latest knowledge and public review sources).
- Or I can give a checklist and script to use when calling for quotes, plus what to expect in each bid so you can compare fairly.

Immediate practical checklist (use this when vetting companies)
1. Licensing & insurance: Ask for license number and proof of liability insurance and worker’s comp.
2. References & reviews: Check Google, Yelp, and BBB reviews; ask for local recent references.
3. Load calculation: Require an ACCA Manual J (not just “rule of thumb”) to size the system correctly.
4. Credentials: NATE certification for technicians is a plus.
5. Written estimate: Get at least 3 written bids with equipment model numbers, SEER rating, total cost, and itemized labor/parts.
6. Permits & inspections: Ensure they will pull required permits and arrange inspections.
7. Ductwork & airflow: Confirm they’ll evaluate and test duct leakage and airflow; ductwork problems should be fixed before installing a new system.
8. Warranty & labor guarantee: Check manufacturer warranty and ask about the contractor’s labor warranty.
9. Rebates & incentives: Ask about utility rebates and any federal/state tax credits for high-efficiency systems.
10. Payment & financing: Confirm deposit amount, payment schedule, and financing options if needed.

Typical cost ranges (Atlanta area, approximate)
- Basic central AC replacement (mid-efficiency, 2.5–3.5 ton): roughly $4,000–$8,000.
- Higher-efficiency systems (16–20+ SEER, variable-speed): $7,000–$12,000+.
- If ducts need major repair or replacement, add several thousand dollars.
(Prices vary widely by brand, equipment size, and installation complexity. Get multiple bids.)

Questions to ask any contractor (short script)
- “Are you licensed and insured in Georgia? Can you provide your license number?”
- “Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and provide the report?”
- “Which equipment models do you recommend and why? What are their SEER/HSPF ratings?”
- “What is included in this price (permit, disposal, new thermostat, line set, refrigerant, startup, testing)?”
- “What warranties do you offer on parts and labor?”
- “Can you show recent local references or online reviews?”

If you want, give me your ZIP code and whether you prefer certain brands or efficiency levels and I’ll suggest 3–5 contractors near you to contact and draft a comparison checklist you can use when you get estimates. Which would you like?
